subject: docs/coop/artifacts/route-b.DR-006.preview-disposition.v2.json
reviewType: independent, refute not confirm; one of three subjects dispatched together
summary: Subject and prompt held at their dispatched digests, both read-only. Every attack axis fails. The sharpest thing in this artifact is also the best: it enumerates twelve parked identities and then refuses to let the enumeration become the boundary. I tested that against file 08, which states under 'Exact DR-006 park coverage' that 'The property also covers unlisted identity-affecting fields' — so the disposition's refusal is not caution for its own sake, it is a correct reading of the row it is dispositioning. All four D-002 rides for this row are named with their consequence, rowQuoted matches file 08 byte-for-byte, and every cited digest matches live bytes.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 28fb23ec9f01de17753624d9e90bec53d75df2344d62594321c17da8a799d161, equal to the prompt's expected value, -r--r--r-- at both ends. I verified the prompt itself against the dispatch-supplied digest 50b49de6… before relying on the subject digests it carries.

The attack 'treats applied EIR v12 as binding recipes / SATISFIED of DR-006' fails. appliedHeadNotThisDisposition pins evidence-identity-recipes.v12.json at f0bfaebd…, which matches live bytes, and states 'Applied lineage head (D-003). Application of a head is not binding per-surface recipes and is not SATISFIED of this row.' whatThisDoesNotDo adds 'Does not bind any identity recipe.'

The park-coverage claim is correct at source, which is the test that mattered most here. The artifact lists twelve parked identities and then states 'File 08 Exact DR-006 park coverage: the property—not this enumeration—is the boundary. This disposition does not close the property by listing members.' File 08's own section reads: 'Freeze §7.1 currently names RunId, sealed-Run semantic-manifest identity, EvidenceDigest, finding fingerprint, FactViewId, cache/regeneration keys, executionPlanCommitment, and subjectScopeCommitment computation/verification. Related named gaps are policyOutcome.derivationDigest and capabilityManifestId. The property also covers unlisted identity-affecting fields.' The disposition's list is a superset of the ten file 08 names, adding the two PlanId-affecting fields, and it disclaims closure by enumeration — which is exactly what a property-bounded row requires.

The attack 'hides D-002 rides' fails. namedD002RidesIfOwnerRecorded carries all four rides D-002 attaches to DR-006, each with its consequence: SARIF for analyze 'DROPS from the preview. RunId and Finding fingerprint stay conceptual'; rebuildable cache/index keys 'Stay conceptual'; Coverage on TS dispatch 'Stays conceptual (subjectScopeCommitment)'; PlanId for the TS role 'Stays conceptual (typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot has no producing rule)'. The symmetry field cites D-002 T2-04 — 'none of these survives on prose' — and whatMustNotBePretendedSettled repeats all four independently.

rowQuoted is faithful, tested by string equality against the live row rather than by reading: the decision text 'Freeze §7.1 identity-recipe property and exact FACT-PLANE closure items remain open' and the owner 'Each identity-owning V1 surface + FACT-PLANE/evidence authorities + coordinator' both match file 08 exactly, and statusAtAuthoring HARD-BLOCKED matches its leading label.

The d070Note claim is true in the edited register. It states 'D-070 appended a preview-scope note to other rows. DR-006 still has no scoped owner-recorded disposition.' file 08's DR-006 cell contains no 'Preview-scope owner recording' note, and D-070's condition-1 snapshot row names DR-006 among the rows that 'remain without SATISFIED or scoped owner-recorded disposition'.

whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA tracks file 08's needs cell — binding recipes, Phase-1A subject-set agreement, declared sufficiency view type and closed rungUnavailableBecause vocabulary, retained negative controls — and improves on it by restating the first item as 'Binding per-surface identity recipes; the §7.1 PROPERTY is the boundary' and adding independent review of those recipes.

The attack 'coordinator becomes recording authority' fails: ownerWhoMustRecord names the file 08 owner and adds 'Coordinator may draft. D-000 does not make the coordinator those identity-owning surfaces.' condition1EffectIfOwnerRecorded adds 'This file existing, or an ACCEPT verdict, is not owner recording', which forecloses this verdict being read as the recording, and whatThisDoesNotDo includes 'Does not owner-record this row.'

The attacks 'silent SATISFIED or condition-1 discharge' and 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' fail: status CANDIDATE-NOT-RECORDED, binds NOTHING, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, reviewStatus AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, condition-1 effect scoped to 'architecture-preview scope only' with 'Conditions 2-5 remain independently required. Condition 5 remains the only authorization for docs/v2/implementation/', and whatThisDoesNotDo refuses both SATISFIED and the implementation directory.

The selection authority is real and correctly characterised: D-069 is ADOPTED at commit 5f6b4e07bb9293041e494ab08d74942878a5af97, which resolves to 'D-069/D-071/D-072: select Route B for DR-006/007/009', and the artifact states that selection 'Writes no disposition. This artifact is that later disposition draft.' whatThisDoesNotDo adds 'Does not re-adopt or overturn D-069.'

The remaining cited digests match live bytes: COORD 2af51835…, file 08 9495c70f… (the post-D-070 value), and the v1 predecessor at 056f94ff…. predecessorChange honestly scopes the delta: 'Retargets selection authority from CONTESTED D-051 to new-cycle D-069. Refreshes live pins after D-070. Adds park-coverage boundary sentence and T2-04 symmetry field. Does not change whatMayBeDesigned or rides.'

whatMayBeDesigned is genuinely bounded rather than permissive: P-006-1 allows a preview analyze/doctor emitting a verdict and D9 exit but forbids 'a durable authoritative record of having gated' and forbids publishing RunId, Finding fingerprint, EvidenceDigest, FactViewId, PlanId or Coverage as settled recipes; P-006-2 allows naming parked fields conceptually but forbids supplying 'a producing rule, computation, or verification recipe and call it settled'.
file 08 is unedited and git reports zero modified tracked files. I wrote three verdict files, one per subject as the prompt directs, and edited and committed nothing.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of this subject. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.
Whether the identity-owning V1 surfaces and FACT-PLANE/evidence authorities would in fact record this. The artifact states its own existence and an ACCEPT are not that recording.
The internal correctness of evidence-identity-recipes.v12. Its digest verifies and I confirmed the artifact treats it as an applied head that closes nothing on this row; I did not audit it.
Freeze §7.1's identity-recipe property itself, beyond confirming file 08's park-coverage section describes it as covering unlisted fields.
Whether Route B is the better choice for DR-006. That was decided by D-069, which is adopted and which this artifact does not re-open.
The Phase-1A subject-set agreement, the sufficiency view type and the rungUnavailableBecause vocabulary, all left owed.

environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256 of the prompt and all three subjects at start and again at end with ls -l for permissions; digest verification of every cited input against live bytes; git log --format=%s at full hash for the selection commit; json parse of the artifact with string-equality comparison of rowQuoted decision and owner against the live file 08 row and of statusAtAuthoring against its leading label; normalised text extraction of file 08's 'Exact DR-006 park coverage' section to test the property-versus-enumeration claim; per-row scan for 'Preview-scope owner recording' cell notes; comparison of whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA against file 08's needs cell; structured checks of status, binds, sealRecommendation, the coordinator-not-authority clause and the whatThisDoesNotDo refusals; git status across the tree

acceptNote: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 advisories. DR-006 is the row where a disposition could most easily launder a list into a closure, because the park is defined by a property and the tempting move is to enumerate its members and call the property covered. This artifact enumerates twelve of them and then says in terms that the enumeration is not the boundary — and file 08 backs that, stating the property 'also covers unlisted identity-affecting fields'. All four D-002 rides are named with their consequences rather than gestured at, and rowQuoted matches the live row by string equality.
